A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VD-RAG poisoning study. All 25 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables, and appendices, support comparison; relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v3 reports original attack and defense evaluations on two ViDoRe datasets, together with appendix ablations, sensitivity analyses, and qualitative examples.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results, including the attack comparisons in Tables 1–4 and supplementary results in the appendices.

M1.justification: The MO-PGD procedure, generation objective, and prompt-based, transfer, ensemble, and adaptive attack variants remain unchanged. The retrieval-loss simplification in Equation 2 leaves its optimization gradients unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions retain ViDoRe-V1-AI and ViDoRe-V2-ESG, with the same targeted and universal attack scenarios and appendix evaluations. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same white-box, transfer, ensemble, and GPT-5/Gemini-2.5-Flash prompt-based comparisons, including the same restricted comparator sets in targeted Settings II–III. Defense comparisons also retain their membership.

E3.justification: Section 3 and the appendices retain the same splits, model configurations, retrieval and generation metrics, 250 optimization steps, batch size of eight, and defense protocols. No new evaluation accompanies the larger-model conjecture.

E4.justification: The ColPali ablation in Table 7, UMAP analysis in Figure 6, perturbation study in Figure 7, defense evaluations, and qualitative examples are unchanged. The new OCR explanation introduces interpretation without an additional diagnostic experiment.

E5.justification: Both versions report five different initial images and the same mean/max aggregation practices. There is no change to repeated-run information or uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1–12 and the empirical figures retain their result entries and values. For example, Table 4 preserves white-box ASR-R@1 of 0.97 for CLIP-L/InternVL3-2B and 0.00 for ColPali/InternVL3-2B. The added scale extrapolation interprets existing evidence.

T1.justification: Equation 2 removes only an image-independent constant: L_R(v3) = L_R(v4) + |Q+| - |Q-|. This is an equivalent optimization objective, with unchanged gradients and minimizers. The remaining mathematical definitions and derivations are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about single-image targeted disinformation, universal denial of service, and the differing vulnerabilities under white-box and black-box access.

C2.justification: Section 4 newly attributes prompt-generated attacks' partial success to typography exploiting OCR capabilities. Expanded limitations in Section 8 explicitly identify open-weight-only evaluation and conjecture success against larger models. These additions qualify and interpret unchanged experiments.

D1.justification: Hyperparameters, appendix prompts, H100 NVL hardware, and approximately 325 GPU hours remain unchanged. The existing code repository address moves to footnote 5; this does not change the stated access or reproducibility information.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning remain unchanged. Bibliography edits add DOI formatting and adjust capitalization and page abbreviations without introducing new related work.

P1.justification: Appendix J becomes Section 8, and Appendix K's ethics discussion moves after the conclusion. v4 adds acknowledgments and a review notice, alongside localized explanatory edits and citation restyling. Most prose and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 receives cosmetic icon and layout changes. The expanded author/affiliation block and relocated sections reflow pages and tables, including Table 1 moving from page 7 to page 8. Empirical displays retain their content and structure.

improvement.justification: v4 makes the limitations more prominent, explicitly clarifies open-weight-only testing, and adds an OCR-based explanation of prompt-generated attacks. These provide modest gains in clarity and scope transparency. The empirical evidence is unchanged, and the added conjecture about larger models remains unvalidated.
